question: Kandinsky painted ten large canvases he called Compositions between 1910 and 1939. How many can be seen today?
answer: Seven. Compositions I, II and III were destroyed in the Second World War and survive only in black-and-white photographs, so their colours are known from studies. The early Kandinsky in the books is partly a reconstruction. A painter obsessed with colour left three of his largest statements as grey photographs.
move: A body of work you can see today may be missing its beginning.
trap: Assuming a famous painter's major works all reached museums.
reference: Hans K. Roethel and Jean K. Benjamin, Kandinsky: Catalogue Raisonné of the Oil Paintings, Volume One 1900-1915, Sotheby Publications, 1982
